description: Get ratio-based peer comparison for a company and its closest competitors. Peers are selected by matching 2-digit SIC industry code. Returns pipeline-computed ratios from up to 10 peers alongside the subject company for direct benchmarking. Ratio categories: profitability, liquidity, leverage, efficiency, per_share, owner_earnings, valuation. TTM (trailing twelve months) ratios are used when available for the most current view. The exact 4-digit code is matched first, then the 3- and 2-digit groupings, with S&P 500 members first within each. Each company appears once, under its main listed share class; a candidate with no figures for the period is left out and counted in peers_omitted_no_data. Without as_of_date, peers are companies listed today. With as_of_date, peers are companies listed on that date — including ones delisted since — ranked by S&P 500 membership on that date, and figures are limited to that date: by SEC acceptance time when the ratio data carries it (_meta.pit_safe=true), otherwise by period end (_meta.pit_safe=false). Available on every plan — sample returns the subset covered by the sample bucket.

as_of_date.description: Historical date (canonical cross-tool date param). Peers are the companies listed on this date, including ones delisted since, ranked by S&P 500 membership on this date. Figures are point-in-time by SEC acceptance time when the ratio data carries it (_meta.pit_safe=true), else limited to periods ending on or before this date (_meta.pit_safe=false).

categories.description: Ratio categories to include in the comparison. Defaults to profitability, valuation, and leverage.

limit.description: Maximum number of peers to return alongside the subject company (1–10). Defaults to 5.

period_end_before.description: Alias of as_of_date (as_of_date preferred — the canonical name). Only include ratios with period_end on or before this date.

ticker.description: Subject company ticker or CIK, e.g. AAPL or '0000320193'. Peers are auto-selected by SIC code.

name: get_peer_comparables

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only tools that have no PAYG-equivalent price.

basis.description: payg_charge = real agent-pay charge. payg_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via PAYG for this call. false = indicative PAYG-equivalent value; your plan already covers this call for free.

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

payg_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for via the agent-pay PAYG flow — the rate-limit / depth-limit checks were bypassed for this call only.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

price_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the price surfaces were last refreshed.

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy

categories.description: Ratio categories included in each peer panel

data.description: One row per company (subject + peers): ticker, cik, name, sector, industry, is_subject, ratios

lineage.description: Provenance for pipeline-derived values (ratio.parquet / factor_scores.parquet): source table + pipeline computed_at, plus a pointer to the tools that return filing-level lineage. NOT point-in-time (recomputed on each pipeline run).

peers_omitted_no_data.description: Candidate peers left out because they had no ratio figures for the period; each was replaced by the next-closest candidate

subject.description: Subject ticker the peer set is built around
